name: Femboy hair dye

card.summary: Pastel or soft-toned hair colouring, often pink, lavender or blue, used as part of femboy styling to give a softer, more feminine look.
card.note: Dark hair usually needs bleaching first, which can damage hair.

quick.overview:
Femboy hair dye refers to colouring hair in soft pastel shades such as pink, lavender or mint as part of femboy style, in which men and boys present with traditionally feminine clothing, makeup and accessories. The colour is meant to complement the softer overall look.

Wikipedia lists hair dye alongside skirts, jewelry and makeup among femboy self-expression, and a femboy fashion site calls pastels the ultimate feminine colours. Stylists describe pastel pink as a current mainstream trend.
quick.how: Pastel shades are produced with semi-permanent dyes, often after lightening dark hair; some people use ombre blends from natural colour to pastel. Hairdressing guides note pastel fades within weeks, typically toward a pale blonde, so colour is refreshed regularly.
quick.risks: Lightening hair first can dry or damage it, and dyes can irritate sensitive scalps; hair product guidance recommends patch testing. Pastel colour fades quickly.

lead: Femboy hair dye is the use of pastel hair colour, commonly baby pink, lavender or soft blue, as part of femboy styling. Wikipedia describes a femboy as a person, usually male, who expresses traditionally feminine traits through clothing, jewelry, makeup or hair dye.[1]
The term combines fem and boy, is dated by Dictionary.com to at least the 1990s, and spread through forums and social media from around 2018 onward.[1]

One femboy fashion site argues that pastels embody softness and calls soft pink the ultimate feminine colour; its only hair suggestion is a gradient from natural colour to pastel.[2] Hair-colour trade coverage describes soft, lived-in pastel pink as a mainstream trend.[3]

chain: Soft colour matches pastel clothing and makeup
angle.text: Pastel colour changes the visible hair tone immediately and is used to match a feminine wardrobe palette. It is easily changed or faded for those who prefer a temporary look.

paras: Pastel shades are lightened, soft versions of saturated colours. Hairdressing guides say dark hair generally has to be lightened before pastel pink will show.[3] Soft shades fade toward a pale blonde as they wash out.[3]

Wikipedia names hair dye among the ways femboys express femininity and notes the term's online spread from 4chan to Reddit and TikTok.[1] A femboy fashion site presents pastels and soft pink as feminine-coded and suggests natural-to-pastel gradients.[2] The proposed femboy flag also uses pink and light blue.[1]
